# Causal result `of`

When an adnominal `of` phrase names the inanimate producer of a result, label it `p.Force, p.Force`: `the rewards of this program`. Establish causation from the noun and context, not from `of` alone. Preserve distinct relations: `Stuart's strategies` is `p.Gestalt, p.Gestalt`; `our business` is `p.OrgMember, p.Possessor`; an animate maker in `your contributions` is `p.Agent, p.Gestalt`; `Each of you` is `p.QuantityItem, p.Whole`; and `proud of your contributions` is `p.Stimulus, p.Topic`. A causal scene role need not imply a Force lexical function: `the devastation of the fire on the town` is `p.Force, p.Gestalt`.

# Circumstantial `with`

When a `with` phrase supplies a background condition or contextual basis for the main assertion, label both its scene role and lexical function `p.Circumstance`. This holds for `cramped and un-ruly with Kumon Parents next door` and `With a Pizza Hut, IHOP, 3 Starbucks, Chilis, Panera, and Chipotle on campus ALONE, VCU has some of the best eating options`. Do not infer `p.Ancillary` merely from the word `with`, clause position, or a human complement. Use `p.Ancillary` when the complement actually accompanies or co-participates with a primary participant; decide from the relation expressed in context.
